newsitem.title: INDIA: New Indian customs offices to help speed air cargo.
newsitem.headline: New Indian customs offices to help speed air cargo.

text.p: India has opened new customs offices and reorganised others across the country to cope with a big growth in air cargo complexes, container depots and container freight stations, customs officials said.

But forwarders expressed disappointment that the timetable to fully computerise customs clearance and linked services by the end of the year has clearly slipped. Dates were given at the time of the budget early this year but officials now publicly admit it will take at least another 12 months.

New offices have been set up in Pune, Mangalore, Trichy, Jodhpur and Amritsar whilst the main offices in the four Metro cities of Mumbai, Delhi, Calcutta and Chennai have been streamlined. Shippers can get easier access directly to senior officers for quick decisions, officials added.
The government has also launched a support operation to help exporters move more quickly to international bar-coding and EDI systems for their products.

The Commerce Ministry said they had set up links with UN-ESCAP and EAN-International Brussels to allocate article numbers and bar codes to individual companies. Shippers said this would speed up air cargo dramatically not only for customs processing but logistics handling, as firms start to use adopt them. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
